description: Figure 5(b) is a line plot illustrating the training loss ratio relative to FLOPs (floating-point operations) for different model architectures. The x-axis, labeled "TFLOPs," represents the cumulative computational cost in trillions of FLOPs, using a logarithmic scale that ranges from 1e7 to 9e8. The y-axis, labeled "Loss Ratio (%)," shows the percentage ratio of the loss value for each method compared to the Vanilla model, ranging from 94% to 100%. Six distinct lines, each with a unique color and marker, represent different methods: Vanilla (purple, circle markers), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue, square markers), SepLLM (n=64) (orange, diamond markers), SepLLM (n=128) (green, triangle-up markers), SepLLM (n=64, H) (red, triangle-down markers), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (black, star markers). The Vanilla model's line remains flat at 100% across all FLOPs. All other methods start below 100% and generally increase toward 100% as FLOPs increase, indicating their loss is initially lower than Vanilla's but converges to it with more computation. The StrmLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=128) lines show a relatively steady climb, while the SepLLM (n=64, H) and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) lines exhibit a more pronounced initial drop before rising, with the latter reaching a peak loss ratio of approximately 99.5% before stabilizing.
